interest: Prewar intelligence on Japanese in Hawaii, including Kilsoo Haan's advocacy.
overview: This file comprises the Department of State Central Decimal File docket list (List of Papers) for file 894.20211A, titled 'Military Affairs: Military Activities of Japan in Hawaii Including Gathering of Information, Espionage, Propaganda' spanning 1932 to 1939. Across nine docket pages, it indexes 58 numbered communications, intelligence reports, cross-references, and memoranda exchanged between the Department of State, War Department (Military Intelligence Division, G-2), Navy Department (Office of Naval Intelligence), Department of the Interior, and members of Congress. Major subjects documented include surveillance of Japanese tankers and training vessels (such as the Taisei Maru and Taiyo Maru) in Hawaiian waters during U.S. naval maneuvers; allegations of subversive indoctrination and cultural nationalism within Hawaiian Japanese language schools; controversies surrounding Pacific-area educational curricula and Helen Pratt's textbook 'Japan: Where Ancient Loyalties Survive'; interdepartmental committee efforts to curb objectionable activities of Japanese naval and civil personnel in Hawaii; intelligence analyses and legislative proposals regarding dual nationality and former Japanese military personnel; extensive anti-Japanese espionage reports submitted by Korean nationalist Kilsoo K. Haan and the Sino-Korean People's League; and legal complications involving Hawaiian territorial court commissions seeking overseas depositions from Japanese diplomatic personnel in South Africa and South America.

subfiles.about: Nine-page Department of State docket sheet and purport list cataloguing correspondence, intelligence reports, and legal inquiries concerning Japanese military, naval, and espionage activities in the Territory of Hawaii from 1932 to 1939.
subfiles.summary: This nine-page List of Papers constitutes the central docket register for Department of State decimal file 894.20211A, indexing 58 numbered entries of official correspondence, military and naval intelligence reports, memoranda, and legal records dating from February 1932 through August 1939. It tracks investigations by the War Department (G-2) and Navy Department (ONI) into suspicious Japanese naval tanker movements, espionage rings, training ship visits, and cultural preservation efforts in Hawaiian language schools. The docket records extensive deliberations concerning educational curricula and Helen Pratt's textbook 'Japan: Where Ancient Loyalties Survive', interdepartmental committee actions on foreign military personnel, and communications from Korean activist Kilsoo K. Haan. Additionally, it indexes legal records regarding commissions from Hawaiian territorial courts to take depositions from Japanese diplomats in South Africa and South America.
